name: Euler ancestral dancing
plain: An Euler ancestral step leaps to a sigma several steps ahead, then a second ancestral step with the same x0 returns to the next planned sigma. With eta_dance above 0, the split collapses: x lands on x0 and is re-noised to the next sigma, based on reading the code. One model call per step.
math: (σ↓,σ↑)=ancestral(σᵢ,σ_{i+leap},η). x+=d·(σ↓−σᵢ)+n·s·σ↑. Then (σ↓₂,σ↑₂)=ancestral(σ_{i+leap},σᵢ₊₁,η_dance); d₂=(x−x0)/σ_{i+leap}; x+=d₂(σ↓₂−σ_{i+leap})+n·s·σ↑₂. η_dance>0: root of a negative gives σ↓₂=0, σ↑₂=σᵢ₊₁, so x=x0+n·s·σᵢ₊₁. η_dance=0: σ↓₂=σᵢ₊₁, no noise. Not danceable near the end falls back to plain Euler ancestral.
label: from code
surprise: The second half-step moves sigma upward (σ_{i+leap} < σᵢ₊₁) while reusing the same x0.

audit.note: Literal formula matches extra_samplers.py:698-714, but σ_leap<σᵢ₊₁ makes core get_ancestral_step take a root of a negative (comfy/k_diffusion/sampling.py:73). By reading, not run: NaN, min() keeps σ↑₂=σᵢ₊₁, σ↓₂=0, so at default eta_dance=1 x lands on x0, then gets noise at σᵢ₊₁. Only eta_dance=0 walks up deterministically.
